nodes.statement: The number of models of random temporal networks proposed in the literature is still limited and no systematic foundations are available . In establishing such foundations, a natural question is: What is the temporal analog of the ErdHos-R\'enyi random graph model? The answer to this question is not unique, as the time dimension can be incorporated in different ways. Some candidates considered in the literature consider a sequence of independent ErdHos-R\'enyi graphs, some others incorporate some dependencies in such a sequence (see for example ).

The graph G_F=(V_F, E_F, lambda_F) is an increasing temporal forest for S, if [(a)] item G_F is a temporal subgraph of G, item the graph F=(V_F, E_F) is a forest (i.e.\ acyclic graph) with |S| components, item for each s in S there is a connected component~T_s of~F such that s~reaches all vertices of~T_s in~G_F.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def: increasing temporal forest}
	Let $\mathcal{G}=(V, E, \lambda)$ be a temporal graph and let $S\subseteq V$ be a set of vertices.
	The graph $\mathcal{G}_F=(V_F, E_F, \lambda_F)$ is an \emph{increasing temporal forest for $S$}, if
	\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
	\item $\mathcal{G}_F$ is a temporal subgraph of $\mathcal{G}$,
	\item the graph $F=(V_F, E_F)$ is a forest (i.e.\ acyclic graph) with $|S|$ components,
	\item for each $s \in S$ there is a connected component~$T_s$ of~$F$ such that $s$~reaches all vertices of~$T_s$ in~$\mathcal{G}_F$.
	\end{enumerate}

  \begin{cases}
    \lambda(e) - Y_{k-1}^{S}, & \quad \lambda(e) \geq Y_{k-1}^{S}\\
    \lambda(e) - Y_{k-1}^{S} + 1, & \quad \lambda(e) < Y_{k-1}^{S}.
  \end{cases}
  \]
  Notice that for any two edges $e,f \in E_k^{S}$ such that $\lambda(f) < Y_{k-1}^{S} \leq \lambda(e)$

  the edge on which the minimum of $w_k^{S}$ is attained, that is,
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:ek_is_argmin}
    e_k^{S}
    = \arg\min \{w_k^{S}(e) \mid e \in E_k^{S} \},
  \end{equation}
  and therefore, for every $k \in [s, n-s - 1]$,
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:Xk}
    X_k^{S}

  \end{equation}

  = 0

nodes.statement: Let p= (1+varepsilon(n))cdot fraclog nn and G sim F_p(K_n). As above, let X be the nodes that can reach between n^1/3log n and n^1/3 + varepsilon(n) vertices in G_[0, p_1] and let Y be the nodes that are reached by between n^1/3log n and n^1/3 + varepsilon(n) vertices in G_[p_2, p_3]. Furthermore, let Z=Xcap Y be their intersection and recall that |Z|ge n - frac2nlog log n with probability at least 1 - frac20 log log nlog n according to~creflemma: almost everyone reaches many. Now, conditioned on the information about the edges appearing in G_[0,p_1] and G_[p_2, p_3], let G'=(V, E') be the static graph with the same node set as G and the edge set E'=\ein binomV2:lambda(e)notin [p_0, p_1]cup [p_2, p_3]\, where lambda is the time label function of G. Note that according to~crefobs: min degree the minimum degree in G' a.a.s.\ is at least n - (log n)^2. Now, let x,yin Z be a fixed ordered pair of vertices. Applying~crefcorollary: target set to HsimF_fracp3(G') with S=A(x), a=2, and T=B(y), we can conclude that A'(x)cap B(y)neq emptyset with probability at least 1 - 3n^-loglog n, and, thus, x reaches y with at least that probability. Hence, after a union bound over all ordered pairs, we get that all nodes in Z reach each other with probability at least 1 - 3n^-loglog n + 2. Therefore, G has a temporally connected component of size at least n - frac2nloglog n = n - o(n) a.a.s.

\label{lem: chernoff}
  Let $X_1,\ldots, X_T$ be independent random variables taking values in $\{0,1\}$, let $X$ denote their sum, and let $\mu=\mathbb{E}[X]$. Then, the following hold:
  \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item\label{chernoff 1} 
    For any $\delta>0$,
    \[
      \mathbb{P}[X\ge (1+\delta) \mu] 
      \le \Big( \frac{e^\delta}{(1+\delta)^{1+\delta}} \Big)^\mu
      \le \exp\Big(-\frac{\mu \delta^2}{2+\delta}\Big).
    \]
    \item\label{chernoff 2}
    For any $R\ge 6\mu$,
    \[
      \mathbb{P}[X\ge R] \le 2^{-R}.
    \]
    \item\label{chernoff 3}
    For any $0<\delta<1$,
    \[
      \mathbb{P}[X\le (1-\delta) \mu] \le \exp\Big(-\frac{\mu \delta^2}{2}\Big).
    \]
  \end{enumerate}
